A Passing Identity

This is an aggressive, pass-leaning attack: +5% pass rate over expected, top of the league's range, and no interest in sitting on a lead (49% pass when ahead).

The Offensive Blueprint

The backfield runs through one man — Chase Brown absorbs 68% of the carries (league ~59%), a true bell-cow share that makes his rushing volume among the safest floors in the sport when the script cooperates.

In the passing game the ball funnels to Ja'Marr Chase — 29% of targets (league ~23%), a genuine alpha share that concentrates the receiving value at the top.

They run downhill — mostly inside the tackles (17% to the edge vs ~25%), a gap/power scheme that trades big plays for a steady, grinding floor.

When they fall behind they abandon the run entirely — 65% pass while trailing, so their pass-catchers have huge comeback-script ceilings.

They live in the shotgun (83% of snaps vs ~68%) — a spread, pass-oriented structure.

The tight end is barely used in the passing game (10% of targets vs ~15%) — fade their TE's receiving props.

By the numbers it's an efficient unit — a 46% success rate (above the 44% average).

In the Red Zone

Their red-zone identity is pass-first (64% pass), which puts scoring equity on Ja'Marr Chase.

Defense — Soft on the Ground

They lock down opposing WR2s — just 22 rec yds/game (vs ~36); fade receiving props there.

Soft against opposing tight ends — 46 rec yds/game (vs ~35). A rec-yards target.

They surrender 137 rushing and 241 passing yards per game (league ~120 / ~230). The run moves against them — target opposing RB1s.

They leak TE touchdowns (0.47/game vs ~0.24) — an anytime-TD spot to attack.

They lock down opposing WR1s — just 53 rec yds/game (vs ~58); fade receiving props there.

They leak RB rushing TDs (0.59/game vs ~0.46) — an anytime-TD spot to attack.

Broadly a leaky unit — 47% success rate allowed (vs ~44%); points come easy against them.

The Betting Angles

Bottom line: Ja'Marr Chase holds value even when they're winning; their pass-catchers have massive ceilings in comeback scripts (fade-material as underdogs); opposing RB1s smash on the ground and at the goal line; opposing TE anytime-TD is a repeatable angle.

Built on 2024–25 data; the profile rebuilds through the season as the current staff and roster set their own tendencies.
